records.paraphrase: The published GPT-2 encoder builds a reversible representation of all 256 byte values as Unicode symbols. Its pretokenization expression separates categories such as letters and numbers before BPE. Within each resulting piece, the encoder chooses the adjacent pair with the smallest learned rank, merges nonoverlapping occurrences and repeats. Encoding converts each piece to UTF-8 bytes before mapping those bytes; decoding joins the token symbols, maps them back to bytes and then decodes the combined byte sequence. Chapter 42 reproduces these operations with a tiny illustrative vocabulary to expose the letter-versus-digit boundary in `a1`. That vocabulary is course-authored and supplies no pretrained GPT-2 token IDs or tokenizer parity result.
